summary: @servicetitan/hammer-react 1.42.7 ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes 727KB opaque payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (hex-prefixed identifiers, rotated string array, numeric-cipher literal table) and, on npm install, downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases for the installer's platform+arch, unzips it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js — a 727 KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle at the tarball root that is also fully obfuscated with a large numeric string table (n7gIxM) and no readable source. The package's declared purpose is a React UI component library, which has no functional need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or an obfuscated multi-hundred-kilobyte install-time payload. package.json's files allow-list is ["dist", "CHANGELOG.md"], yet setup.mjs and math_init.js appear at the tarball root — the payload is not part of the author's declared publish surface. The combination of preinstall-triggered acquisition of an alternate runtime, execution of an opaque bundled blob whose behavior is intentionally unreadable, purpose mismatch with a React UI kit, and files-allow-list mismatch is consistent with a compromised-publish supply-chain attack: installing this version runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's host at install time before any application code executes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
